title: Jurisdictional handshake proxy for EU dataflow routing constraints
creator: Nina Patel
description:
Goal: implement a jurisdictional 'handshake proxy' layer in the request router that enforces EU-only/data-residency constraints, evaluates per-customer allowlists/denylists, selects tiered model variants, and emits decision telemetry for audit and debugging.

Background: customers can declare EU residency requirements at account or token scope. Runtime must ensure requests that are marked EU-only never leave EU zones and must fallback deterministically to approved model variants when capacity or tier restrictions apply. This work adds a constrained, auditable decision path rather than relying on ad-hoc fallbacks spread across services.

Scope of this ticket:
- New middleware in the routing service called 'jurisdictional-handshake' that consults the policy cache and the account allow/deny lists.
- Deterministic fallback order: 1) pinned region-local model (customer override), 2) Dedicated EU pool compatible model variant, 3) Hosted EU model with telemetry-tagged quantized variant, 4) emergency escape (non-EU) only with dual-approval and audit escrow.
- Emit a structured decision event for every request: decision, applied policy key, model variant chosen, reason code, TTL for cached decision. These events stream to audit-logs and the observability pipeline.
- Admin APIs for allowlist/denylist changes scoped to customer and org; changes propagate to policy cache with bounded staleness (configurable TTL).
- Canary rollout plan with opt-in list and metric gates.

Design constraints & trade-offs:
- We will keep decision logic out of the hot per-token path where possible by using a lightweight cache keyed by (account_id, policy_version, region). Heavy-weight evaluation runs in the control-plane on policy changes.
- To minimize latency, the middleware will attach routing hints (X-Redwood-Routing-Decision) for downstream dequeueing rather than forcing synchronous lookups during model allocation when a cached decision exists.
- The emergency escape path is intentionally gated: enabling it increases availability at cost of compliance risk. We require explicit audit and a two-person approval recorded in the audit stream before any single request uses escape.

Implementation notes:
- Add new protobuf messages for DecisionEvent (flat fields only) and update the audit export to include them.
- Policy cache will be a low-latency in-memory store with per-key TTL and change-notification coming from control-plane pub/sub.
- Allow/deny lists stored in control-plane DB with an endpoint to fetch deltas.
- Routing service will tag decisions with short-lived signed tokens to allow downstream model servers to validate origin of routing hint.

Acceptance tests (high-level):
- Simulate account with EU-only flag, verify no request is routed to non-EU model variants under normal operations.
- Exhaust Dedicated EU pool and verify deterministic fallback to hosted EU model with expected decision telemetry emitted.
- Attempt an emergency-escape without approval and assert request denied; repeat with dual-approval and assert allowed and audited.

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag gated. Stage 1: rollout to 1% of EU accounts, observe routing metrics and audit volume for 48h. Stage 2: 10% with stricter metric thresholds. Stage 3: opt-in for enterprise accounts, then gradual ramp to 100% with a 7-day observation window per stage.

Docs and artifacts: Confluence design + policy matrix (link below), initial PR for middleware skeleton, test harness for residency simulation.

Open questions:
- TTL tuning for policy cache vs control-plane change load (initial default 60s).
- Exact schema for DecisionEvent (needs security review for PII/PIA).
- Should allowlist changes support immediate revocation (push) vs eventual consistency?

Next steps:
- Create protobufs and audit event schema (owner: Marco).
- Implement middleware skeleton and fakes for integration tests (owner: Ashwini).
- Coordinate security review with Compliance and ProdSec (owner: Nina).

acceptance_criteria: All EU-only flagged requests must have a DecisionEvent emitted to audit-stream
Fallback order must be deterministic and documented: pinned -> dedicated EU -> hosted EU quantized -> emergency escape
Emergency escape cannot be used without recorded dual-approval; attempts are denied and logged
Policy changes (allowlist/denylist) propagate to routing decision within configured TTL and produce change events
Routing decision latency p50 delta < 6ms vs baseline when cache hit
DecisionEvent schema reviewed and approved by Security and Compliance
